examples.en: On busy days I eat convenience food for dinner.
The convenience store's ready meals have become really varied.
You just heat the convenience food in the microwave.
I live alone, so I often buy ready meals.
The ready-meal market is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 간편식은 맛도 괜찮고 값도 싸요.
examples.en: This ready meal tastes decent and is cheap too.

explain: 도시락, 즉석밥, 냉동식품처럼 빠르고 쉽게 먹을 수 있게 만든 음식이에요. 뉴스에서는 '간편식 시장'처럼 소비 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '즉석식품', '편의점 도시락'처럼 구체적으로 말해요.
explain_en: It covers foods made to be eaten quickly and easily, such as lunch boxes, instant rice and frozen food. In the news it appears in consumer talk such as '간편식 시장'. In daily speech people are more specific, saying '즉석식품' or '편의점 도시락'.

examples.en: When kimchi-making season comes, the price of napa cabbage goes up.
My family gathers every kimchi-making season.
The market is really crowded during kimchi-making season.

examples.ko: 김장철을 맞아 마트에서 소금 할인을 해요.
examples.en: For kimchi-making season, the supermarket is discounting salt.
I ordered chili powder to get ready for kimchi-making season.
This year even during kimchi-making season, the weather is warm.

explain: 겨울을 대비해 김치를 많이 담그는 늦가을 무렵을 말해요. '철'은 '휴가철', '장마철'처럼 어떤 일이 많은 시기를 뜻하고, 짝말로 '김장하다', '김장 김치'가 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to the late-autumn period when people make a lot of kimchi to prepare for winter. '철' means a season when something is common, as in '휴가철' and '장마철', and related words are '김장하다' and '김장 김치'.

examples.en: You must cook raw meat before eating it.
I wonder if it's okay to give raw meat to a cat.
Wash your hands right away after touching raw meat.
I use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables.
The fridge smells like raw meat.
I ate raw meat by mistake and got a stomachache.

explain: '날-'은 익히지 않은 것에 붙어요. 날달걀, 날것처럼 짝으로 같이 알아 두세요. 불에 익힌 고기는 '익힌 고기'라고 하고, 날고기는 '생고기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '날-' attaches to things that are not cooked, as in 날달걀 and 날것. Cooked meat is '익힌 고기', and raw meat is also called '생고기'.

en: gamey smell; smell of raw meat

examples.ko: 고기를 구울 때 누린내가 나서 환기를 했어요.
examples.en: The meat gave off a gamey smell when grilling, so I aired out the room.

examples.ko: 양고기는 누린내 때문에 못 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people can't eat lamb because of its gamey smell.

examples.ko: 생강을 넣으면 고기 누린내를 없앨 수 있어요.
examples.en: Adding ginger can get rid of the gamey smell of meat.

examples.ko: 이 집 곰탕은 누린내도 안 나고 국물이 깔끔해요.
examples.en: This place's beef bone soup has no gamey smell and the broth is clean.

examples.ko: 누린내 제거에는 우유에 담그는 방법도 있어요.
examples.en: Soaking in milk is another way to remove the gamey smell.

examples.ko: 염소 고기 특유의 누린내가 익숙하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm not used to the gamey smell typical of goat meat.

explain: '비린내'는 생선 냄새이고 '누린내'는 고기나 털에서 나는 냄새예요. 요리할 때는 '잡내'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: '비린내' is the smell of fish, while '누린내' is the smell that comes from meat or animal hair. When cooking, people also say '잡내'.

examples.en: I bought deodeok at the market and grilled it to eat.

examples.ko: 더덕은 향이 진해서 좋아하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Deodeok has a strong aroma, and many people like it.

examples.ko: 어머니가 더덕구이를 해 주셔서 밥을 두 그릇 먹었어요.
examples.en: My mother made grilled deodeok, so I ate two bowls of rice.

examples.ko: 더덕 껍질을 벗기는 게 은근히 힘들어요.
examples.en: Peeling deodeok is surprisingly hard.

examples.ko: 산에서 캔 더덕이라 향이 훨씬 좋아요.
examples.en: It's deodeok dug up in the mountains, so the aroma is much better.

examples.ko: 고추장 양념을 바른 더덕이 밥반찬으로 딱이에요.
examples.en: Deodeok with a red pepper paste marinade is perfect as a side dish for rice.

explain: 껍질을 벗겨 두드려서 구이나 무침으로 많이 먹어요. 쓴맛과 진한 향이 있어서 '더덕구이'처럼 양념을 해서 먹는 경우가 많아요. 비슷한 뿌리채소 '도라지'와 함께 한식에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People usually peel it, pound it, and eat it grilled or as a seasoned side dish. It has a slightly bitter taste and a strong aroma, so it is often cooked with seasoning, as in '더덕구이'. It often appears in Korean food together with another root vegetable, '도라지'.

examples.en: I was away for a few days, and the plant pot dried up completely.
If you leave bread out, it dries up and gets hard.
I found a shriveled, dried-up tangerine in the fridge.

examples.ko: 김치 위쪽이 말라비틀어지기 전에 빨리 드세요.
examples.en: Please eat the kimchi quickly before the top dries out.
In the drought, all the grass ended up withered and dry.

examples.ko: 화분 속 잎이 말라비틀어져서 결국 버렸어요.
examples.en: The leaves in the pot dried up and shriveled, so I finally threw it away.

explain: 그냥 '마르다'보다 심해서 오그라들고 볼품없어진 느낌이 있어요. 식물, 빵, 과일처럼 물기가 빠진 것에 많이 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰면 매우 거친 말이 돼요. 활용은 '말라비틀어져요, 말라비틀어진'이에요.
explain_en: It is stronger than plain '마르다' and suggests something that has shriveled up and looks poor. It is common for plants, bread and fruit that lost their moisture, and sounds very harsh if used about people. It conjugates as '말라비틀어져요' and '말라비틀어진'.

examples.en: The baby is crying for food, probably because he's hungry.
Time for your food, sweetie.

examples.ko: 맘마 다 먹고 나면 같이 놀아요.
examples.en: When you finish your food, let's play together.
The child said 'mamma,' the baby word for food, for the first time.
My little nephew smiles whenever he sees his food.
Let's wash your hands before you eat.

explain: 어린아이에게 '밥'을 가리킬 때 쓰는 아기 말이에요. 어른끼리 이야기할 때는 쓰지 않고, 아이에게 말하거나 아이 이야기를 할 때 귀엽게 써요. '까까'(과자)도 같은 종류의 아기 말이에요.
explain_en: It is baby talk for '밥' (food or a meal) used with small children. Adults don't use it with each other; you use it when talking to a child or cutely about a child. '까까' (snacks) is another word of the same kind.

examples.en: The persimmon is so ripe that it's mushy.
The banana is mushy, so I don't want to eat it.

examples.ko: 발밑에서 물컹한 느낌이 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I felt something squishy under my foot and was startled.
If you overcook eggplant, the texture turns mushy.
Please cook it just lightly so it doesn't get mushy.
The tofu I froze and thawed was mushy.

explain: 푹 익은 과일이나 삶은 채소처럼 눌러 보면 속이 무르게 들어가는 느낌이에요. 부드러운 것과 달리 식감이 별로라는 말투로 쓸 때가 많아요. '말랑하다'는 귀엽고 부드러운 느낌이라 쓰임이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It describes the feeling of overripe fruit or boiled vegetables, where the inside gives way when pressed. Unlike simply 'soft', it is often said with a sense that the texture is unpleasant. '말랑하다' feels cute and soft, so its use is a bit different.

examples.ko: 밀알 한 알이 땅에 떨어져 싹이 텄어요.
examples.en: A single grain of wheat fell to the ground and sprouted.
The farmer carefully sowed wheat grains in the field.
Birds are pecking at the wheat grains.

examples.ko: 이 빵은 밀알이 그대로 씹혀서 고소해요.
examples.en: You can chew the whole wheat grains in this bread, so it tastes nutty.

examples.ko: 작은 밀알도 모이면 큰 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: Even small grains of wheat become a great force when they gather.

examples.ko: 밀알처럼 작은 도움이 세상을 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: Small help, like a grain of wheat, can change the world.

explain: 밀의 낟알 하나하나를 말해요. 작지만 싹이 터서 열매를 맺는 모습 때문에 비유로도 쓰여요. '쌀알'처럼 '-알'이 붙은 말과 같은 방식이에요.

phrases.en: I also want to be a grain of wheat for society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 위해 작지만 소중한 힘을 보태는 사람이 된다는 뜻으로, 다짐이나 연설에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means becoming someone who contributes a small but precious effort for others, and is used in resolutions or speeches.

explain_en: It refers to each individual kernel of wheat. Because a small kernel can sprout and bear fruit, it is also used figuratively. It is formed like '쌀알', with '-알' attached.

examples.en: Table manners education starts at home.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 밥상머리에서 휴대폰을 안 봐요.
examples.en: In our house, we don't look at phones at the dinner table.
Grandfather always taught us manners at the dinner table.
Please don't talk about that kind of thing at the table.

examples.ko: 밥상머리 대화가 아이에게 큰 도움이 된대요.
examples.en: They say conversation at the dinner table helps children a lot.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 밥상머리에서 들은 말이 아직도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember what I heard at the dinner table as a child.

explain: '밥상머리 교육'처럼 식사 자리에서 어른에게 배우는 예절과 대화를 말할 때 많이 써요. 밥상 위의 음식이 아니라 밥 먹는 자리 그 곁을 가리켜요. 그냥 식탁을 말할 때는 '식탁'이나 '밥상'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is often used in '밥상머리 교육', meaning the manners and talk children learn from elders at mealtime. It points to the place beside the table where people eat, not the food on it. For the table itself, people just say '식탁' or '밥상'.

examples.ko: 아이 입가에 밥풀이 하나 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a grain of rice stuck at the corner of the child's mouth.

examples.ko: 손에 붙은 밥풀을 떼어 내기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to get the rice stuck on my hand off.
I sealed the envelope with a few grains of rice.

examples.ko: 설거지할 때 그릇에 말라붙은 밥풀은 물에 불려요.
examples.en: When I wash dishes, I soak the dried-on rice grains in water.

examples.ko: 옷에 밥풀 묻은 줄도 모르고 하루 종일 다녔어요.
examples.en: I went around all day without noticing there was rice on my clothes.

examples.ko: 김밥을 싸다 보니 손이 밥풀투성이가 됐어요.
examples.en: While rolling gimbap, my hands ended up covered in rice.

explain: '밥알'과 거의 비슷하지만, 입가나 손, 옷에 붙어 있는 밥 한 톨을 말할 때 특히 잘 써요. '입가에 밥풀이 묻었어요'처럼 '붙다·묻다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It is close to '밥알', but it is especially natural for rice stuck to the mouth, hands or clothes. It often goes with verbs like '붙다' and '묻다', as in '입가에 밥풀이 묻었어요'.

examples.en: Sea water is salty because its salt content is high.
The doctor told me to reduce my salt intake.

examples.ko: 라면 국물에는 염분이 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Ramen broth has a lot of salt in it.
Farming is hard on land with a lot of salt.
When you sweat, salt leaves your body too.

examples.ko: 이 간장은 염분이 적어서 건강에 좋아요.
examples.en: This soy sauce is low in salt, so it's healthy.

explain: '소금'은 우리가 직접 뿌려 먹는 재료이고, '염분'은 음식이나 바닷물에 들어 있는 소금 성분이에요. 건강 이야기에서는 '염분을 줄이다', '염분을 섭취하다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '나트륨'은 영양 표시에 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: 소금 is the ingredient you sprinkle, while 염분 is the salt component inside food or sea water. In health talk you say 염분을 줄이다 or 염분을 섭취하다. 나트륨 is the term you see on nutrition labels.

en: have a light bite; stave off hunger

examples.en: When I was hungry, I had a quick bite with some bread.
I'll have some gimbap to tide me over and then go.

examples.ko: 요기할 만한 게 없어서 편의점에 들렀어요.
examples.en: There was nothing to snack on, so I stopped by a convenience store.

examples.ko: 손님이 오기 전에 떡으로 요기해 두세요.
examples.en: Have some rice cake to tide you over before the guests arrive.

examples.ko: 오래 걸릴 테니 먼저 요기부터 하세요.
examples.en: It will take a while, so grab a bite first.
It was just to tide me over, so I didn't eat much.

explain: 배가 너무 고프지 않게 조금만 먹을 때 써요. '식사하다'는 한 끼를 제대로 먹는 것이고, 요기하다는 간단히 때우는 쪽이에요. '요기를 하다'처럼 '요기'만 써도 돼요. '여기'의 말투인 '요기'와는 다른 낱말이에요.
explain_en: Use it when you eat just a little so you aren't too hungry. 식사하다 is eating a proper meal, while 요기하다 is getting by with something small. You can also say 요기를 하다. It is a different word from the 요기 that means 여기.

examples.ko: 영화 볼 때 주전부리를 사 갈까요?
examples.en: Shall we buy some snacks to bring when we watch the movie?

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에 가면 주전부리가 항상 많아요.
examples.en: There are always lots of snacks at Grandma's house.
I eat fruit or nuts as snacks.

examples.ko: 밤에 주전부리 때문에 자꾸 살이 쪄요.
examples.en: I keep gaining weight because of late-night snacking.
Snacking is really hard to quit.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 주전부리도 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always pack snacks too.

explain: 끼니 사이에 입이 심심해서 이것저것 먹는 과자, 과일 같은 간식을 말해요. '간식'보다 가볍고 친근한 느낌이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '군것질'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the snacks, such as crackers or fruit, that you nibble on between meals when your mouth feels bored. It sounds lighter and more casual than '간식'. '군것질' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 이 과자에는 첨가물이 거의 안 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This snack has almost no additives in it.

examples.ko: 식품 첨가물은 포장지 뒤에 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: Food additives are listed on the back of the package.
I bought juice with no additives.

examples.ko: 아이에게 첨가물 많은 음식을 주고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to give my child food full of additives.

examples.ko: 화학 첨가물을 줄이는 회사가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More companies are cutting back on chemical additives.
The taste turned a bit strange because of the additives.

explain: '재료'는 음식의 기본이 되는 것이고, '첨가물'은 맛이나 색, 보관을 위해 따로 더한 것이에요. 포장지에서 '식품 첨가물', '무첨가'라는 말을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: 재료 is what a dish is basically made of, while 첨가물 is something added separately for taste, color or storage. You often see 식품 첨가물 and 무첨가 on packaging.
